objects.canonical_term: Gordman Properties v. Hall County Board of Equalization
objects.summary: Nebraska case authority for using county board proceedings to challenge actual value, uniformity, or both.
objects.plain_language: A taxpayer can argue that a property is valued too high, unequally valued compared with similar property, or both.

relationships.note: Protest hearing may include actual value and equalization arguments.

source_refs.citation: Gordman Props. v. Hall Cty. Bd. of Equal., 1987 Neb. Supreme Court text via Justia.

objects.canonical_term: Kearney Convention Center v. Buffalo County Board of Equalization
objects.summary: Nebraska case authority for the principle that reasonable valuation classifications and methods must still produce uniform and proportionate results not exceeding actual value.
objects.plain_language: Different property types can be valued with different methods, but the resulting values still have to fit Nebraska's uniformity and actual-value requirements.

facts.object: Reasonable classifications and different valuation methods must be correlated to uniform, proportionate, non-excessive values.

relationships.note: Links method choice to constitutional equality.
Valuation method choice cannot defeat uniformity.

source_refs.citation: Kearney Convention Ctr., Inc. v. Buffalo Cty. Bd. of Equal., 216 Neb. 292 (1984), secondary text via vLex.

objects.canonical_term: Lancaster County Board of Equalization v. Moser
objects.summary: Nebraska Supreme Court decision addressing the high burden for an equalization claim based on comparison to another property's erroneous undervaluation.
objects.plain_language: Pointing to one neighbor's mistake is usually not enough; the taxpayer must prove a grossly excessive value caused by intentional conduct or failure of a plain legal duty, not a mere judgment error.

facts.object: systematic intentional/failure-of-duty error from mere error of judgment

relationships.note: Defines evidentiary burden for equalization relief.
Relevant to evidence quality in protest hearing.

source_refs.citation: Lancaster Cty. Bd. of Equal. v. Moser, 312 Neb. 757 (2022).

objects.canonical_term: Lincoln Telephone & Telegraph Co. v. County Board
objects.summary: Nebraska case authority discussing substantial compliance with equalization and uniformity where designed or manifest departures from rules are avoided.
objects.plain_language: Nebraska courts recognize that assessment is approximate, but intentional or major departures from equalization rules can matter.

relationships.note: Case involved tangible personal property comparison.

source_refs.citation: Lincoln Tel. & Tel. Co. v. County Board, Nebraska Supreme Court text via Justia.

objects.summary: Nebraska's core real-property valuation concept: actual value is market value in the ordinary course of trade for taxation purposes.
objects.plain_language: The assessor is trying to estimate what the property would sell for in an ordinary market, as of the assessment date, subject to Nebraska law.

relationships.note: Ratio studies compare assessed/appraised value to sale prices as market indicators.
Actual value is not the same as tax due.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-112.
Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.

objects.summary: Value placed on property for assessment purposes before levy application and credits; generally tied to actual value except where Nebraska law provides a different assessment basis.
objects.plain_language: This is the value number on the assessment side of the tax system; it is not the tax bill.

relationships.note: Combined with levy to compute taxes.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1301.

objects.summary: Nebraska real and personal property assessment is anchored to January 1 at 12:01 a.m. for listing and valuation unless a specific statute provides otherwise.
objects.plain_language: The yearly value question is normally: what was the property as of January 1?

dates.description: Assessment of real and personal property.

relationships.note: Real property list and value statute.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Property Assessment and Taxation Calendar.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1301.

objects.summary: CAMA is the assessment-office data and modeling environment used to maintain property characteristics, stratify property, and support mass appraisal estimates.
objects.plain_language: CAMA is the assessor's structured property database plus valuation modeling tools.

relationships.note: IAAO mass appraisal standard includes data and system expectations.
Property record is core CAMA unit.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.
Nebraska DOR PAD, Title 350 regulations index.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in Nebraska PAD ratio context
objects.summary: Ratio-study uniformity statistic measuring average percentage dispersion of ratios around the median ratio.
objects.plain_language: COD shows how tightly individual assessment ratios cluster around the typical ratio. Lower usually means more uniform within the tested group.

thresholds.note: IAAO Ratio Study Standard gives COD ranges by property type and market homogeneity.

relationships.note: COD is a common horizontal equity statistic.
COD is centered on median ratio.
PRD addresses vertical equity signals rather than general dispersion.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
IAAO, Glossary for Property Appraisal and Assessment.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in ratio studies
objects.summary: Statistical interval used to express uncertainty around an estimated ratio-study statistic or level indicator.
objects.plain_language: A confidence interval says the data give a range, not just one exact answer.

relationships.note: Ratio study interpretation should consider uncertainty.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

objects.summary: Valuation approach that estimates value from land value plus depreciated improvement cost; commonly relevant to newer improvements, special-use property, or where market/income evidence is limited.
objects.plain_language: Estimate the land, estimate what the building would cost, subtract depreciation, then reconcile with market evidence.

relationships.note: One of the major appraisal approaches.
Improvement cost is adjusted for depreciation.
Land component often comes from land schedules/tables.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Court Case Summaries History.
IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in Nebraska valuation practice
objects.summary: Adjustment to improvement cost or value for loss in utility, condition, age, functional inadequacy, or external market factors.
objects.plain_language: Depreciation is how the system accounts for a building not being worth the same as brand-new cost.

relationships.note: Condition and quality influence depreciation modeling.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.summary: A derived burden measure comparing property taxes to property value; useful for taxpayer explanations and regressivity/incidence analysis.
objects.plain_language: It answers: what share of the property's value is paid as tax for the year?

relationships.note: Effective burden is central to regressivity analysis.

source_refs.citation: Christopher R. Berry, Reassessing the Property Tax (2021).
Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.

objects.summary: Process of aligning assessment levels and treatment so property is valued uniformly and proportionately under Nebraska constitutional and statutory requirements.
objects.plain_language: Equalization is the correction layer that tries to make similarly situated property carry a fair share of the tax base.

relationships.note: County board can correct over/under valuation in protest/equalization session.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Const. art. VIII, § 1.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1504.
Nebraska TERC, About Us.

objects.canonical_term: Agricultural and Horticultural Land Special Valuation
objects.summary: Nebraska special valuation program for qualifying agricultural or horticultural land, distinct from ordinary market/actual-value treatment.
objects.plain_language: Some qualifying agricultural or horticultural land can be assessed under a special valuation framework rather than the same basis as ordinary real property.

relationships.note: Moser involved agricultural land valuation/equalization dispute.
Different statutory treatment from general real-property actual value.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1359.
Nebraska DOR PAD, Title 350 Chapter 14 index entry.

objects.summary: Assessment equity principle that similar properties should be assessed similarly relative to market value.
objects.plain_language: Similar properties should receive similar assessment treatment.

relationships.note: COD is a standard dispersion metric.
Maps appraisal theory to Nebraska legal requirement.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Neb. Const. art. VIII, § 1.

objects.summary: Nebraska statutory property tax relief program for qualifying owner-occupants, administered under the homestead exemption statutes and PAD calendar/guidance.
objects.plain_language: Homestead exemption can reduce property tax burden for eligible homeowners, but it is different from proving the assessed value is wrong.

relationships.note: Exemption eligibility is separate from contesting value.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, PAD Calendars.
Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.

objects.summary: Valuation approach that derives value from income-producing capacity; Nebraska law specifically references income approach and discounted cash-flow analysis for certain commonly owned vacant subdivision lots.
objects.plain_language: For income-producing property, value can be estimated from income. Nebraska also has a specific statute for certain subdivision lots.

facts.object: certain vacant or unimproved lots in same subdivision/tax district held for sale or resale

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1314.
IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in Nebraska valuation practice
objects.summary: Structured schedule used to value land units by market area, use, size, location, or other land attributes.
objects.plain_language: A land table is how the assessor's system turns land characteristics into a land value estimate.

relationships.note: Land tables are often market-area sensitive.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.summary: Overall relationship between assessed/appraised values and market value for a studied class, commonly represented by median or other ratio-study level measures.
objects.plain_language: Level of value asks whether a class is generally assessed at, below, or above the target percentage of market value.

relationships.note: Median is a common level statistic.
Weighted mean supports PRD and aggregate burden analysis.
PAD R&O uses indicated level of value by class/county.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Nebraska DOR PAD, 2025 Annual Report.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in Nebraska mass appraisal
objects.summary: Geographic or economic segment where properties compete in a similar market and share valuation influences.
objects.plain_language: A market area groups properties that buyers tend to compare with one another.

relationships.note: Neighborhood coding is often a local implementation of market segmentation.
Market areas can define ratio-study strata.
Comparable sale selection often considers market area.

source_refs.locator: location data and market area discussion
source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in ratio studies
objects.summary: Arithmetic average of assessment ratios; useful but more sensitive to extreme ratios than the median.
objects.plain_language: The mean ratio is the ordinary average of all ratios in the group.

relationships.note: Median is less affected by outliers.
Weighted mean accounts for price/value weights.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

objects.summary: Middle assessment ratio in an ordered ratio-study sample; commonly used to indicate appraisal level because it is less influenced by outliers.
objects.plain_language: If you sort all assessment ratios, the median is the middle one.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Nebraska DOR PAD, 2025 Annual Report.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in county CAMA systems
objects.summary: CAMA/location code grouping properties with similar market influences for modeling, review, and comparable-sale selection.
objects.plain_language: Neighborhood codes help the assessor compare a property to the right local market.

relationships.note: Neighborhood is a local coding form of market segmentation.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.
Lancaster County, Property Valuation Protests.

objects.summary: Nebraska taxable personal property generally refers to depreciable tangible personal property with Nebraska net book value greater than zero, subject to statutory exemptions and filing rules.
objects.plain_language: Business equipment and similar depreciable tangible property may need to be reported even though licensed vehicles, livestock, and some other property are excluded.

relationships.note: Personal property may use net book/depreciation framework.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1201.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in IAAO ratio studies
objects.summary: Ratio-study vertical-equity statistic estimating whether assessment ratios systematically change as property values change.
objects.plain_language: PRB checks whether higher-value properties tend to be assessed at lower or higher percentages than lower-value properties.

relationships.note: Negative or positive patterns may indicate regressivity/progressivity depending on ratio orientation.
PRD is a descriptive ratio of means; PRB is regression-oriented.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
IAAO, Glossary for Property Appraisal and Assessment.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in IAAO ratio studies
objects.summary: Vertical-equity indicator calculated as mean ratio divided by weighted mean ratio; values materially above or below 1 can suggest regressivity or progressivity patterns.
objects.plain_language: PRD compares a simple average ratio to a value-weighted ratio to see whether lower- and higher-priced properties are treated differently.

thresholds.note: Common IAAO acceptable PRD range referenced in ratio-study practice; verify jurisdiction-specific application before legal use.

relationships.note: Research cautions about vertical inequity measures.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Lincoln Institute, Measures of Vertical Inequality in Assessments.

objects.summary: Structured record of parcel identity, land, improvement, location, use, quality, condition, ownership, and valuation data used by an assessment office.
objects.plain_language: The property record is the assessor's factual data file for the parcel.

relationships.note: CAMA stores and maintains property records.
Record errors can be evidence in valuation discussions/protests.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.
Lancaster County, Property Valuation Protests.

objects.summary: Nebraska refundable income tax credit and related property-tax relief framework for qualifying school district and community college property taxes, with eligibility varying by tax year.
objects.plain_language: Some Nebraska property taxes may create a state income tax credit, but the qualifying taxes and years matter.

facts.object: Form PTC or PTCX depending on year/status

relationships.note: Credits may reduce/refund burden but are not the same as assessment value.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Tax Credit General Information.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in county CAMA systems
objects.summary: CAMA data elements describing construction quality, condition, effective age, and physical/functional state of improvements.
objects.plain_language: Quality and condition codes are how the assessor's database describes how well-built and how worn a structure is.

relationships.note: Quality and condition affect depreciation estimates.
Property record should preserve characteristic data.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.

objects.summary: Pattern where lower-priced properties are assessed at higher percentages of market value than higher-priced properties, shifting relative tax burden downward.
objects.plain_language: Regressivity means lower-value homes carry a higher assessment percentage than higher-value homes.

relationships.note: Regressivity is a vertical equity failure mode.

source_refs.citation: Christopher R. Berry, Reassessing the Property Tax (2021).
McMillen & Singh, Assessment Regressivity and Property Taxation (2019/2020).
IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

objects.summary: Practice risk where sold properties are selectively adjusted to sale price while unsold properties are not similarly reviewed, potentially invalidating ratio studies and creating inequity.
objects.plain_language: Sales chasing is treating sold properties differently just because they sold.

relationships.note: Can bias sale sample and ratio study.
Selective treatment can create unequal assessment.
IAAO standard discusses sales validation and study integrity.

source_refs.locator: sales validation and ratio study integrity
source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Nebraska DOR PAD, Title 350 Chapter 12 index entry.

objects.summary: Valuation approach estimating property value from sales of comparable properties adjusted for relevant differences.
objects.plain_language: Find similar sold properties, adjust for differences, and use them to support a market value estimate.

relationships.note: Comparable sales should be valid market indicators.
Recent arms-length comparable sales can support protest evidence.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Court Case Summaries History.
Lancaster County, Property Valuation Protests.

objects.summary: Ratio formed by dividing assessed or appraised value by a sale price that has been validated and adjusted as needed for ratio-study use.
objects.plain_language: A sales ratio compares the assessor's value to what the property sold for.

relationships.note: Median ratio computed from sales ratios.
COD computed from sales ratio dispersion.

source_refs.locator: ratio formation and market value discussion
source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).
Nebraska DOR PAD, Title 350 Chapter 12 index entry.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in ratio studies
objects.summary: Whether the sale sample is large, representative, and reliable enough to support level and uniformity conclusions for a class or stratum.
objects.plain_language: A ratio study is only as reliable as the sales data behind it.

relationships.note: More strata can reduce sample size.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

objects.summary: Dividing properties or sales into meaningful groups by property type, location, value range, market area, valuation group, or other characteristics for analysis.
objects.plain_language: Stratification keeps unlike properties from being mixed in a way that hides problems.

relationships.note: Nebraska/PAD workflow may use valuation groups.
More granular strata may reduce sample size.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

source_refs.locator: Reports and Opinions / Sales File chapters
source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Title 350 regulations index.

objects.summary: Tax amount produced after assessed values are certified, levies are set by authorized taxing authorities/county board workflow, and statements are delivered for treasurer collection.
objects.plain_language: Your value is only one part of the bill. Levy rates, local budgets, credits, and exemptions also affect taxes due.

relationships.note: Tax bill is not the assessed value.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1601.

objects.summary: Nebraska constitutional requirement that real property taxes be levied by valuation uniformly and proportionately, except where the Constitution or Legislature permits different treatment.
objects.plain_language: The tax base must treat comparable property evenhandedly under Nebraska's constitutional framework.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Const. art. VIII, § 1.
Lancaster Cty. Bd. of Equal. v. Moser, 312 Neb. 757 (2022).

objects.summary: Sale screened and qualified as a reliable market indicator for appraisal, comparable-sale analysis, or ratio-study use.

objects.summary: Grouping of properties used for valuation, ratio-study analysis, or Reports and Opinions review; exact definitions should be extracted from PAD R&O and Title 350 materials.

objects.summary: Assessment value and property tax due are related but distinct: value establishes a tax-base share, while levies, budgets, exemptions, and credits determine the final tax bill.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1601.

objects.summary: Assessment equity principle that lower- and higher-value properties should not be systematically assessed at different percentages of market value.
objects.plain_language: A low-value home and a high-value home should not be assessed at systematically different percentages just because of price level.

objects.jurisdiction: General assessment; used in ratio studies
objects.summary: Ratio of total assessed/appraised value to total sale price for the sample, giving more influence to higher-value sales.

relationships.note: PRD compares mean and weighted mean.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

Neb. Const. art. VIII, § 2.

objects.canonical_term: County Board of Equalization Protest Hearing Workflow
objects.summary: Workflow for county board review of filed protests, assessor/referee reporting, hearing, board decision, notice, and potential TERC appeal.
objects.plain_language: After a protest is filed, the county board considers evidence and issues a decision that can be appealed.

steps.step: Receive filed protest with required property description, requested value, reasons, and signature.
Assessor/referee prepares report and recommendation if applicable.
County board hears or considers protest evidence.
Board decides current-year assessed value and mails notice.
Aggrieved party may appeal to TERC under applicable deadline.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1504.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1502.
Sarpy County, Form 422 - Property Valuation Protest.

objects.summary: Operational workflow for maintaining property characteristics, location, quality/condition, land, improvement, sale, and valuation data in a CAMA system.
objects.plain_language: Good assessments depend on keeping parcel data current and auditable.

steps.step: Collect or verify property characteristics.
Update property record fields and coding.
Maintain sales, land, improvement, quality, and condition data.
Run review/quality-control checks before valuation and notices.
Preserve audit/change history for defensibility.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Mass Appraisal of Real Property.
Nebraska DOR PAD, Property Assessment Regulations - Title 350.

objects.canonical_term: Levy Setting and Tax Statement Cycle
objects.summary: Workflow connecting political subdivision budgets/tax requests, county board levy action, tax list creation, county treasurer tax statements, and collection/delinquency dates.
objects.plain_language: Values become taxes only after local budgets and levies are applied.

steps.step: Political subdivisions adopt/file budgets and property tax requests.
County board of equalization levies necessary taxes by statutory deadline.
Assessment/tax records and tax list are prepared/transcribed.
County treasurer collects real property taxes.
Delinquency dates apply by county category.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1601.

objects.summary: Workflow for using qualified sales to compute ratios, level, uniformity, and vertical-equity statistics that inform assessment quality review and equalization.
objects.plain_language: A ratio study checks whether assessments line up with market sales for groups of properties.

steps.step: Collect and validate sales.
Stratify by property class, market area, valuation group, or other relevant criteria.
Compute sales ratios and level metrics.
Compute uniformity and vertical-equity metrics.
Interpret results for equalization, model review, or oversight.

source_refs.citation: IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

objects.summary: Annual Nebraska workflow for listing, valuing, updating, noticing, and certifying real property assessment values.
objects.plain_language: Each year starts with the January 1 property snapshot and moves through assessor updates, notices, protests, equalization, and tax-list steps.

steps.step: List and value real property as of January 1.
Update/revise assessment roll during statutory calendar window.
Send valuation change notices where required.
Handle taxpayer protests during June filing period.
Finalize values for levy/tax-list workflow.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Property Assessment and Taxation Calendar.
Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.

objects.canonical_term: Sales File to Ratio Study Workflow
objects.summary: Workflow moving recorded sales through validation/qualification into ratio-study datasets used for level, uniformity, and equalization analysis.
objects.plain_language: Sales are screened before they become evidence in a ratio study.

steps.step: Collect sales records.
Screen for arms-length/market validity and required adjustments.
Code sale usability and property characteristics.
Assign sales to classes/strata/valuation groups.
Compute ratios and study statistics.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR PAD, Property Assessment Regulations - Title 350.
IAAO, Standard on Ratio Studies (2013).

aliases: Tax Equalization and Review Commission appeal
objects.summary: Workflow for appealing county board of equalization valuation, assessment, or taxation decisions to the Nebraska Tax Equalization and Review Commission.
objects.plain_language: After the county board decision, eligible parties can appeal to TERC by the applicable deadline.

steps.step: Receive county board decision/notice.
Determine appeal eligibility and deadline.
File TERC appeal petition and required materials.
Proceed through TERC review/hearing process.
Commission decision may be subject to judicial review under applicable law.

relationships.note: County board decision is prerequisite for regular protest appeal.
TERC also has statewide equalization role.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska TERC, Appeal Process.
Nebraska TERC, About Us.
Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1504.

objects.summary: Taxpayer workflow from valuation notice or assessment roll review through filing a timely real property valuation protest with required content and evidence.
objects.plain_language: If you disagree with value, gather evidence and file the protest by the deadline with the county clerk/board workflow.

steps.step: Review valuation notice/property record.
Identify issue: market value, data error, classification, or equalization.
Gather evidence such as recent arms-length sales, appraisal, income/cost data, or record corrections.
File Form 422/422A with required requested value, reasons, property description, and signature by deadline.
Proceed to county board protest hearing/review.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-1502.
Nebraska DOR PAD, Real Property Valuation Protest Information Guide.
Lancaster County, Property Valuation Protests.
